rated_messages.input_message: Practice going 10 minutes without smoking. Think of it just as practice. When the urge passes, reward yourself with a break from work or dinner from your favorite restaurant!
When you are stressed, it is easy to focus on the things that are going wrong. Take a few moments to focus on 5 things that have gone well or that you are thankful for this week.
You spent a long time training your brain to want a cig. Now you're retraining your brain, and it's natural that this might take time.
If you miss doing something with your hands, try turning a coin or pen over and over with your fingers.
Ask yourself, "What do I need right now? Is it really a smoke, or is there something else I need? How can I best take care of myself right now?"
If you get urges, remind yourself that cigarettes did that to you. If you go back to them, they will keep making you suffer. Now you are breaking free.
Take a minute to notice what the urge feels like in your body without smoking a cigarette. Notice what is going on. See what happens. Does the urge pass?
You cant always control when you will see other people smoking. But you can control how you respond to your urge when you do.
It's normal to have some doubts during a quit attempt. Keep your quit reasons on hand to remind yourself if ever you feel uncertain or undecided.
Acknowledge your unhelpful thought by writing it down on a piece of paper. Then let it be on it's way by crumpling it up and tossing it in a trash can.
